items.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the biological process of reproduction?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the process by which living beings produce identical copies of themselves without variations.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a biological process by which living beings produce new individuals of their own kind.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a process that occurs only in multicellular organisms to ensure the survival of the individual.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a mechanism by which organisms increase their lifespan continuously.

items.answer: Reproduction is a fundamental biological process through which living organisms produce new individuals of their own kind. It ensures the continuity of life on Earth, allowing species to persist over generations. While it does not increase an individual’s lifespan, it guarantees that life continues even after the parent organisms age and eventually die.

items.stem: A horticulturist performs the plant propagation procedure shown in the diagram. When this newly formed plant matures and bears fruit, which plant’s genetic characteristics will the fruit primarily express, and why?

options.label: A
options.text: Plant Q, because the root system provides all nutrients required for fruit development.

options.label: B
options.text: Plant P, because the upper scion portion dictates the formation of flowers and fruits.

options.label: C
options.text: A blend of P and Q, because their vascular tissues have permanently fused together.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither, because this specific method only produces sterile vegetative leaf growth.

items.answer: In grafting, the upper stem (scion, Label P) determines the genetic characteristics of the shoot system, including leaves, flowers, and fruits. The lower stem (stock, Label Q) merely provides the root system for water and nutrient absorption. Therefore, the fruits will express Plant P’s traits, not Q’s or a blend.

items.stem: In vegetative propagation, plants like Bryophyllum can sprout new plants without producing seeds. Which part of the Bryophyllum plant is responsible for sprouting tiny plantlets?

options.label: A
options.text: Fleshy underground stem

options.label: B
options.text: Root nodules

options.label: C
options.text: Leaves

options.label: D
options.text: Apical meristem

items.answer: In certain plants like Bryophyllum, vegetative propagation occurs through the leaves. The margins of the leaves sprout tiny plantlets, which can eventually drop off and grow into independent, new plants. This is a natural method of asexual reproduction where only one parent is involved, producing genetically identical offspring without the need for seeds.

items.stem: A student observed the growth of Rhizopus (bread mould) under different environmental conditions over a period of 5 days. Based on the documented observations, which combination of environmental factors is most favorable for the rapid germination of fungal spores? Setup Bread Condition Temperature (°C) Relative Spore Growth (Day 5) Setup 1 Dry 30 None Setup 2 Moist 5 Very low Setup 3 Moist 30 Very high Setup 4 Dry 5 None

options.label: A
options.text: Spore formation requires low temperature and dry conditions to prevent spoilage.

options.label: B
options.text: Spores germinate most effectively in the presence of both moisture and warm temperatures.

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature has no effect on mould growth as long as the bread remains moist.

options.label: D
options.text: Moisture is the sole limiting factor for asexual reproduction in simple fungi.

items.answer: Maximum spore germination occurs exclusively when both moisture and warm temperatures (30°C) are provided simultaneously. When either adequate moisture or warmth is absent, fungal growth is severely stunted or completely non-existent. This confirms that these two specific environmental factors are absolutely essential for the rapid asexual reproduction of bread mould.

items.stem: While observing the technique of cutting in a field, at what approximate angle should the stem cuttings be inserted into the soil mixed with compost?

options.label: A
options.text: 15–30 degrees

options.label: B
options.text: 45–60 degrees

options.label: C
options.text: 75–90 degrees

options.label: D
options.text: 90–120 degrees

items.answer: According to the agricultural practices described for cutting, the prepared stem cuttings should be inserted into the soil mixed with compost at an angle of about 45 to 60 degrees from the soil surface. This specific orientation helps the cutting establish roots properly and facilitates optimal exposure to required nutrients and moisture from the soil.

items.stem: In the process of grafting, two plants are involved to create a new plant structure. Which of the following accurately describes the components used?

options.label: A
options.text: Both plants must be wild varieties with strong root systems.

options.label: B
options.text: A healthy stem piece (graft) is inserted into a slit created on a rooted plant.

options.label: C
options.text: Two stem pieces are tied together and planted directly into the soil.

options.label: D
options.text: The rooted plant provides the apical meristem for tissue culture propagation.

items.answer: Grafting involves taking a healthy rooted plant and creating a wound or slit on its twig. A healthy stem piece from another desirable plant variety is then inserted and fitted into this slit. The joint is protected and allowed to heal, resulting in the successful combination and growth of the two distinct plant parts together.

items.stem: Which of the following is the primary advantage of propagating plants using the tissue culture technique?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires minimal scientific equipment and can be done openly in fields.

options.label: B
options.text: It uses the apical meristem to produce healthy, virus-free plantlets ensuring high yields.

options.label: C
options.text: It naturally introduces wide genetic variations in crop plants like bananas.

options.label: D
options.text: It allows the direct fusion of male and female gametes in a laboratory setting.

items.answer: Tissue culture has revolutionized farming practices, particularly for crops like bananas. By using the shoot tip, or apical meristem, farmers can be provided with healthy, mass-produced plantlets. This specific technique is highly effective as it helps eliminate virus-infected plants, thereby ensuring robust growth and significantly higher yields in agricultural production.

items.stem: Based on the provided diagram, which label correctly identifies the specific structure where the zygote will initially form following the event indicated by the dashed line?

options.label: A
options.text: Structure W

options.label: B
options.text: Structure X

options.label: C
options.text: Structure Y

options.label: D
options.text: Structure Z

items.answer: The diagram illustrates a pistil with pollen tube growth. The dashed line indicates the pollen tube delivering male gametes down the style to the ovule (Label Z) located inside the ovary (Label Y). Fertilisation, which is the fusion of gametes, occurs specifically inside the ovule, where the zygote initially forms.
items.concept: Pollen tube growth and male gamete

items.stem: During the observation of yeast under a microscope after incubating it in a warm sugar solution, what indicates that the yeast is actively reproducing?

options.label: A
options.text: The formation of a protective cyst around a single parent cell.

options.label: B
options.text: The fusion of two separate yeast cells to form a zygote.

options.label: C
options.text: The emergence of small, round outgrowths or buds from the parent cells.

options.label: D
options.text: The breakdown of a single yeast cell into multiple identical fragments simultaneously.

items.answer: Yeast reproduces asexually through a process known as budding. When placed in a warm and favorable sugar solution, yeast cells become active and begin to duplicate. This is visible under a microscope as small, round outgrowths, called buds, emerging from the parent cells, which eventually enlarge and separate to live independently.

items.stem: Fungi like Rhizopus grow rapidly on moist bread. Identify the specific structures responsible for this widespread and rapid reproduction.

options.label: A
options.text: Gametes formed in the hyphae

options.label: B
options.text: Tiny round spores formed inside a sac-like structure

options.label: C
options.text: Small buds that detach from the fungal stem

options.label: D
options.text: Vegetative branches that layer into the bread surface

items.answer: Fungi such as Rhizopus reproduce asexually through spore formation. They possess thread-like structures ending in round sacs. Inside these sacs, millions of tiny, lightweight spores are produced. When released, these single-celled spores float easily through the air and germinate quickly upon settling on a moist, nutrient-rich surface like fresh bread.

items.stem: In all the asexually reproducing organisms discussed, the central process behind this type of reproduction is mitosis. What is the immediate consequence of this mechanism for the offspring?

options.label: A
options.text: They possess half the number of chromosomes as the parent.

options.label: B
options.text: They are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones.

options.label: C
options.text: They exhibit high genetic variation essential for evolution.

options.label: D
options.text: They require two parents to contribute genetic material equally.

items.answer: Asexual reproduction relies entirely on mitosis, a type of cell division that produces daughter cells with the exact same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. Consequently, the offspring generated through these methods are genetically identical to the single parent organism. These genetically uniform individuals are scientifically referred to as clones.
items.concept: Mitosis is basis of asexual reproduction

items.stem: Assertion (A): Refrigeration of perishable food prevents their spoilage from moulds and bacteria. Reason (R): Lower temperatures slow down or completely stop the reproduction and growth of spores present in the air.
items.assertion: Refrigeration of perishable food prevents their spoilage from moulds and bacteria.
items.reason: Lower temperatures slow down or completely stop the reproduction and growth of spores present in the air.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false but R is true

items.answer: The assertion is true as refrigerating food greatly extends its shelf life by preventing microbial spoilage. The reason is also true and directly explains the assertion. Spores require warmth and moisture to germinate. Lowering the temperature through refrigeration removes the necessary warmth, effectively slowing or halting the reproduction of moulds and bacteria.

items.stem: A field researcher documented the presence of reproductive organs in the flowers of four different plant species. Which of the following conclusions can be correctly drawn regarding the reproductive capabilities of these specific species? Plant Species Presence of Stamen Presence of Pistil Species W Present Absent Species X Present Present Species Y Absent Present Species Z Present Present

options.label: A
options.text: Only Species W and Y possess the necessary structures to undergo self-pollination.

options.label: B
options.text: Species X and Z are structurally capable of successfully performing self-pollination.

options.label: C
options.text: Species W represents a female flower and must strictly undergo cross-pollination.

options.label: D
options.text: Species Y produces distinct pollen grains but cannot ultimately form a mature fruit.

items.answer: Self-pollination requires the direct transfer of pollen from an anther to the stigma within the same flower. Only species possessing both male (stamen) and female (pistil) reproductive parts can achieve this. Species lacking either part are unisexual and fundamentally incapable of self-pollination, relying entirely on cross-pollination to reproduce successfully.

items.stem: Arrange the following steps of the layering method in the correct chronological sequence. 1. Water the buried twig regularly and observe the growth of new leaves. 2. Select a flexible, thin twig of a tree or a shrub. 3. Cut the rooted twig from the parent plant to grow as a new plant. 4. Bury the middle part of the twig under the soil surface. 5. Wait for roots to develop from the buried area of the twig.
items.answer: In layering, one first selects a flexible twig (2). Next, the middle part is buried under the soil (4). The area is watered regularly to encourage growth (1). After some days, roots develop from the buried section (5). Finally, the newly rooted twig is detached from the parent plant (3).

items.stem: Who among the following scientists proved that new life always comes from preexisting life, strengthening the germ theory of disease?

options.label: A
options.text: P. Maheshwari

options.label: B
options.text: Louis Pasteur

options.label: C
options.text: Subhash Mukhopadhyay

options.label: D
options.text: Gregor Mendel

items.answer: Louis Pasteur conducted pivotal experiments proving that new life arises only from pre-existing life, effectively disproving the long-held belief in spontaneous generation. His ground breaking work significantly strengthened the germ theory of disease and eventually led to modern, essential practices like food preservation and the rigorous sterilization of medical instruments.

items.stem: Why might an organism reproducing exclusively through asexual reproduction be at a disadvantage in a rapidly changing environment?

options.label: A
options.text: Asexual reproduction produces offspring much slower than sexual reproduction.

options.label: B
options.text: The offspring lack genetic variation, making adaptation to new conditions difficult.

options.label: C
options.text: Asexual reproduction requires excessive energy to find a suitable mate.

options.label: D
options.text: The offspring always have half the chromosome number, leading to weakness.

items.answer: Asexual reproduction produces clones, meaning offspring are genetically identical to the parent. While this allows for rapid population growth in stable conditions, it becomes a disadvantage in changing environments. The lack of genetic variation means that if a new disease or environmental stress occurs, the entire uniform population may be wiped out.

items.stem: Identify the correct specific sites for the production of female gametes and the implantation of a developing embryo, respectively.

options.label: A
options.text: Gamete production at N; Implantation at M

options.label: B
options.text: Gamete production at O; Implantation at M

options.label: C
options.text: Gamete production at O; Implantation at N

options.label: D
options.text: Gamete production at M; Implantation at P

items.answer: The ovary (Label O) is responsible for gametogenesis in females, producing mature eggs (gametes). After fertilisation in the fallopian tube (Label N), the zygote undergoes divisions and travels to the uterus (Label M). Here, it implants into the thickened inner lining of the uterus to develop into a foetus.

items.stem: In sexual reproduction, a biological problem arises if both parents contribute their full set of chromosomes to the offspring. How is this problem solved in nature?

options.label: A
options.text: By replacing mitosis with a special cell division called vegetative propagation.

options.label: B
options.text: By a special type of cell division called meiosis that halves the chromosome number.

options.label: C
options.text: By doubling the chromosome number in every generation to maintain stability.

options.label: D
options.text: By destroying half the chromosomes immediately after fertilization occurs.

items.answer: If offspring received full chromosome sets from both parents, the chromosome number would continuously double every generation. Nature solves this through meiosis, a specialized cell division that reduces the diploid chromosome number to half, creating haploid gametes. When these gametes fuse, the original diploid number is correctly restored in the zygote.

items.stem: Humans have 46 chromosomes in their regular body cells. Following meiosis, how many chromosomes does every normal human gamete (sperm or egg) contain?
items.answer: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs. During the process of meiosis, these pairs separate so that each resulting gamete receives exactly one chromosome from every pair. Therefore, a normal human gamete, whether a sperm or an egg, carries exactly 23 chromosomes, ensuring proper genetic transmission upon fertilization.

items.stem: In flower buds, the coloured projections are usually covered by a thin, flat, green covering. What is this outermost whorl of the flower called?

options.label: A
options.text: Petal

options.label: B
options.text: Stigma

options.label: C
options.text: Sepal

options.label: D
options.text: Anther

items.answer: Before a flower blooms, its delicate internal parts are enclosed in a bud. The outermost whorl of this bud consists of a thin, flat, leaf-like green covering designed to protect the developing structure. This protective green layer is called a sepal, which safely guards the colorful petals and reproductive organs inside.

items.stem: Consider the following characteristics related to pollination strategies in plants. 1. Pollen grains are light, small, and produced in huge numbers. 2. Flowers are brightly coloured and produce sweet nectar. 3. The stigma is long and feathery to trap pollen. 4. Pollen grains are large, sticky, or spiny. Which combination of statements correctly represents the features of insect-pollinated plants?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 3

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 4

items.answer: Insect-pollinated plants must attract specific pollinators. To achieve this, their flowers are typically brightly coloured and produce nectar (Statement 2). Furthermore, their pollen grains are large, sticky, or spiny so that they can easily adhere to the bodies of visiting insects (Statement 4). Statements 1 and 3 describe wind-pollinated plants.

items.stem: Match the parts of a flower in List-I with their correct description in List-II. List-I (Flower Part) List-II (Description) P. Stamen 1. Female part comprising stigma, style, and ovary Q. Pistil 2. Swollen base containing ovules R. Anther 3. Male part consisting of filament and anther S. Ovary 4. Produces pollen grains containing male gametes
items.answer: The stamen (P) is the male reproductive part (3). The pistil (Q) is the female reproductive part consisting of three components (1). The anther (R), located at the tip of the stamen, specifically produces the pollen grains (4). The ovary (S) is the swollen base of the pistil containing the ovules (2).

items.stem: In an experimental setup to study pollination in pea plants, stamens are carefully removed from a juvenile flower bud, and the bud is wrapped in a muslin cloth bag. What is the primary purpose of this procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the flower from undergoing any form of photosynthesis.

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure that natural self-pollination occurs undisturbed.

options.label: C
options.text: To prevent self-pollination and control the source of pollen reaching the stigma.

options.label: D
options.text: To protect the stamens from being eaten by pollinating insects.

items.answer: Removing stamens from a juvenile flower bud ensures that the flower cannot self-pollinate. Wrapping the emasculated flower bud in a muslin cloth bag prevents unwanted pollen from wind or insects from reaching the stigma. This controlled technique allows researchers or breeders to manually introduce specific, desired pollen for artificial hybridisation experiments.

items.stem: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between self-pollination and cross-pollination?

options.label: A
options.text: Self-pollination requires external agents, while cross-pollination happens spontaneously.

options.label: B
options.text: Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, whereas cross-pollination involves a different plant of the same type.

options.label: C
options.text: Self-pollination produces fruits, while cross-pollination only produces vegetative growth.

options.label: D
options.text: Self-pollination involves the transfer of eggs, whereas cross-pollination involves the transfer of pollen.

items.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma. If this transfer happens within the same flower or between flowers on the same individual plant, it is termed self-pollination. In contrast, cross-pollination occurs when pollen is successfully transferred from the anther of one plant to the stigma of another plant.

items.stem: Following successful fertilisation in a flowering plant, specific floral parts transform to support seed dispersal and growth. Identify the correct pair representing this post-fertilisation transformation.

options.label: A
options.text: Ovary develops into a seed; Ovule develops into a fruit

options.label: B
options.text: Ovary develops into a fruit; Ovule develops into a seed

options.label: C
options.text: Stigma develops into a fruit; Style develops into a seed

options.label: D
options.text: Anther develops into a fruit; Pollen tube develops into a seed

items.answer: After fertilisation occurs, the flower undergoes significant changes. The ovules, which contain the fertilised egg (zygote), gradually develop and mature into seeds. Concurrently, the thick ovary surrounding these ovules enlarges and transforms into a fruit. This fruit ultimately protects the enclosed seeds and greatly assists in their eventual dispersal across different environments.
items.concept: Ovary and ovules become fruit and seeds

items.stem: What biological process is represented by “Event E” at Day 14, which directly triggers the subsequent maintenance of the uterine lining thickness?

options.label: A
options.text: Shedding of the unfertilized egg and blood vessels

options.label: B
options.text: Release of a mature egg from the ovary

options.label: C
options.text: Implantation of the fertilised zygote into the uterine wall

options.label: D
options.text: Rapid cellular division of the zygote to form an embryo

items.answer: Event E at day 14 represents ovulation, the release of a mature egg from the ovary. Following ovulation, the uterine lining reaches maximum thickness and is enriched with blood vessels to prepare for potential embryo implantation. If implantation (Option C) does not occur, the lining eventually sheds (Option A).

items.stem: Assertion (A): Sexual reproduction in plants creates genetic variation among the offspring. Reason (R): The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete brings together unique combinations of chromosomes from two different parents.
items.assertion: Sexual reproduction in plants creates genetic variation among the offspring.
items.reason: The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete brings together unique combinations of chromosomes from two different parents.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false but R is true

items.answer: The assertion is true because sexual reproduction indeed leads to genetic variation. The reason correctly explains this phenomenon: the process involves the fusion of haploid male and female gametes during fertilisation. This merging combines unique chromosomal combinations derived through meiosis from two distinct parents, resulting in genetically diverse and adaptable offspring.

items.stem: Choose the correct sequential order of steps involved in the process of artificial hybridisation in agricultural crop production. 1. Manual transfer of desired pollen to the stigma 2. Removal of stamens from the flowers 3. Selection of plants with desirable characters 4. Covering the flower with a bag to prevent self-pollination
items.answer: Artificial hybridisation begins with the careful selection of parent plants possessing desirable traits (3). Next, stamens are removed from the selected female parent’s flowers to avoid unwanted self-pollination (2). The emasculated flower is then securely covered with a bag (4). Finally, desired pollen is manually transferred onto the receptive stigma (1).

items.stem: Which Indian scientist is highly recognized as the ‘Father of Indian Embryology’ and developed the technique of in-vitro fertilisation in flowering plants?

options.label: A
options.text: Subhash Mukhopadhyay

options.label: B
options.text: Louis Pasteur

options.label: C
options.text: P. Maheshwari

options.label: D
options.text: Gregor Mendel

items.answer: P. Maheshwari is widely celebrated as the ‘Father of Indian Embryology’. He was a pioneering scientist who successfully developed the complex technique of in-vitro fertilisation in flowering plants. By artificially fusing an egg and a male gamete in a test tube, he laid the foundation for creating new, valuable hybrid plant varieties.

items.stem: Based on the data comparing wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated plants, why do wind-pollinated grasses produce significantly more pollen grains per flower (5,00,000–10,00,000) compared to insect-pollinated plants (20,000–40,000)?

options.label: A
options.text: Wind-pollinated plants require more pollen to feed the insects that visit them.

options.label: B
options.text: Wind is a highly directed and efficient agent that guarantees every pollen grain reaches a stigma.

options.label: C
options.text: Wind pollination is a random process with a lower probability of success, requiring massive pollen production to ensure fertilization.

options.label: D
options.text: Insect-pollinated plants naturally lack the biological capacity to produce large quantities of pollen.

items.answer: Wind pollination relies entirely on random air currents, making it highly inefficient since most pollen is lost and never reaches a compatible stigma. To counter this low probability of success, wind-pollinated plants must produce enormous quantities of lightweight pollen, maximizing the slim chances that a few grains will successfully land and fertilize.

items.stem: Botanists catalogued the structural adaptations of three different flowering plants to understand their primary methods of transferring genetic material. Based on the structural traits, identify the most likely agents of pollination for Plant P and Plant Q respectively. Plant Type Pollen Characteristics Stigma Characteristics Nectar Production Plant P Light and dry Long and feathery Absent Plant Q Sticky and spiny Flat and sticky Present Plant R Large and heavy Short and concealed Present

options.label: A
options.text: Plant P: Wind, Plant Q: Insects

options.label: B
options.text: Plant P: Water, Plant Q: Wind

options.label: C
options.text: Plant P: Insects, Plant Q: Wind

options.label: D
options.text: Plant P: Insects, Plant Q: Water

items.answer: Specific structural adaptations dictate the mode of pollination. Light, dry pollen and feathery stigmas are classic features for wind pollination, allowing grains to be caught by air currents. In contrast, sticky pollen, sticky stigmas, and nectar production are specialized traits designed to attract insects, ensuring pollen successfully attaches to their bodies.

items.stem: Variation among individuals is considered crucial for the survival of a species over long periods. How does sexual reproduction primarily contribute to this survival advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: By ensuring that every offspring is identical, preserving the best traits perfectly.

options.label: B
options.text: By helping some individuals adapt better to changing environmental conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: By increasing the total number of chromosomes in every successive generation.

options.label: D
options.text: By eliminating all genetic defects through spontaneous mutations.

items.answer: Sexual reproduction continuously generates unique genetic combinations through meiosis and gamete fusion. This inherent variation means that within a population, certain individuals may possess traits better suited to survive unexpected environmental shifts, new diseases, or harsh conditions. Thus, variation acts as a vital buffer, helping the species adapt and avoid complete extinction.

items.stem: Many aquatic animals like frogs and fish exhibit external fertilisation. What is the primary cause for these animals producing vastly larger numbers of eggs compared to animals with internal fertilisation?

options.label: A
options.text: They have unlimited internal space to store thousands of developing embryos.

options.label: B
options.text: External fertilisation offers extreme protection, so they maximize offspring production.

options.label: C
options.text: A large number of eggs are destroyed by water currents or eaten by predators.

options.label: D
options.text: Their eggs contain no yolk and require immediate external nutrition to survive.

items.answer: In external fertilization, eggs and sperm are released openly into the water. This environment is highly hazardous, as countless eggs are routinely washed away by strong currents or consumed by various aquatic predators. To ensure that at least a few offspring survive to maturity, these animals must produce enormous quantities of eggs.
items.concept: Many eggs compensate for external loss

items.stem: According to the variations in reproductive strategies among animals, identify the incorrect statement regarding the correlation between the mode of fertilisation and offspring survival.

options.label: A
options.text: Fish rely on external fertilisation and have a very low estimated survival rate of young ones.

options.label: B
options.text: Birds use internal fertilisation and exhibit a moderate to high survival rate of their young.

options.label: C
options.text: Frogs utilize internal fertilisation and produce 5,000 to 50,000 eggs at a time.

options.label: D
options.text: Lizards have internal fertilisation, produce fewer eggs, and show moderate offspring survival.

items.answer: The statement regarding frogs is factually incorrect based on the reproductive data. Frogs are amphibians that rely on external fertilisation, releasing thousands of eggs directly into the water where they meet sperm. Because of this external, unprotected method, the resulting young ones face extremely high mortality rates and low overall survival chances.

items.stem: What is the primary function of the specific device depicted inside the uterine cavity?

options.label: A
options.text: It acts as a mechanical barrier covering the cervix to prevent sperm entry into the vagina.

options.label: B
options.text: It systematically alters hormonal balances to completely stop the ovaries from releasing mature eggs.

options.label: C
options.text: It prevents unwanted pregnancy by acting as an Intra-Uterine Device that interferes with sperm and implantation.

options.label: D
options.text: It provides a permanent surgical block by physically cutting and tying off the fallopian tubes.

items.answer: The diagram illustrates a Copper-T, an Intra-Uterine Device (IUD) placed inside the uterus. It prevents pregnancy by altering the uterine environment, often through released ions, which impedes sperm movement and prevents embryo implantation. It is not a barrier method (Option A), an oral hormone pill (Option B), or surgery (Option D).

items.stem: Arrange the intermediate developmental stages of a butterfly’s life cycle in the correct chronological sequence, starting from the egg. 1. Pupa 2. Adult butterfly 3. Egg 4. Larva
items.answer: The life cycle of a butterfly begins with an egg (3). The egg hatches into a feeding stage called a larva or caterpillar (4). Once enough nutrition is accumulated, it transforms into a resting, transitional stage known as a pupa (1). Finally, it emerges from the pupa as a fully formed adult butterfly (2).

items.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the nourishment of developing embryos in animals. 1. In birds, the egg contains enough yolk to nourish the embryo until it hatches. 2. In mammals, the zygote grows and develops inside the female body, drawing nourishment directly. 3. In fish and amphibians, the mother’s body provides a continuous supply of yolk throughout development. Which of the given statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: Statements 1 and 2 accurately describe embryo nourishment in birds and mammals, respectively. Statement 3 is incorrect because fish and amphibians produce thousands of eggs simultaneously. A mother’s body cannot physically supply large quantities of yolk for so many embryos; instead, the minimal yolk only sustains the embryo until it hatches into a larva.
items.concept: Yolk-rich eggs in reptiles and birds

items.stem: A scientist observes the eggs of an unknown animal species. The eggs are laid in hundreds but contain only a very small amount of yolk. Based on the reproductive strategies studied, what is the most likely developmental pathway for this species?

options.label: A
options.text: The egg will directly hatch into a fully mature, miniature adult.

options.label: B
options.text: The egg will hatch into an intermediate feeding stage (larva) to gain further nutrition.

options.label: C
options.text: The embryo will remain dormant in the egg for several years until external nutrients arrive.

options.label: D
options.text: The egg will require immediate internal fertilisation by a male after being laid.

items.answer: When eggs are produced in massive numbers with minimal yolk, the stored nutrition is insufficient for complete development. Therefore, the egg hatches early into a larva. This intermediate stage is essentially a feeding phase, where the organism consumes organic waste to accumulate enough energy before transforming into its final adult form.

items.stem: Biological data was collected regarding the reproductive strategies of four distinct animal species. Analyzing these evolutionary strategies, which species is most likely to have the highest survival rate for its young ones, and for what biological reason? Animal Species Mode of Fertilisation Average Number of Eggs per Cycle Embryo Protection Level Species K External 10,000 None (released directly in water) Species L Internal 5 Hard protective shell covering Species M Internal 1 Develops inside mother’s body Species N External 500 Soft jelly-like covering

options.label: A

items.answer: Internal fertilisation combined with internal embryonic development provides the maximum physical protection and sustained nourishment against external environmental hazards and predators. While producing fewer eggs, this advanced reproductive strategy ensures the highest probability of survival for the offspring compared to methods involving external fertilisation or laying vulnerable eggs in water.

items.stem: The male reproductive system in humans consists of several highly specialized organs. Which specific structure is responsible for both the production of sperm and the secretion of hormones that regulate physical changes during puberty?

options.label: A
options.text: Vas deferens

options.label: B
options.text: Prostate gland

options.label: C
options.text: Testis

options.label: D
options.text: Urethra

items.answer: The testes are the primary reproductive organs in human males. Located in the scrotum, they perform dual critical functions: producing male germ cells known as sperm, and secreting hormones like testosterone. These hormones not only regulate ongoing sperm production but also trigger the significant physical transformations boys experience during the onset of puberty.

items.answer: The assertion correctly states that testes are housed in the scrotum. The reason is also factually correct and perfectly explains the assertion. Optimal spermatogenesis (sperm production) cannot occur at the standard core body temperature. The scrotum provides an environment that is slightly cooler, making it essential for the development of healthy, viable sperm.

items.stem: A medical chart outlines the standard physiological phases of a typical 28-day human menstrual cycle. What would be the immediate physiological consequence if fertilisation does not successfully occur after the events of Day 14? Phase (Days) State of Uterine Lining Major Biological Event Days 1–5 Shedding and breaking down Menstrual bleeding occurs Days 6–13 Gradually rebuilding thickness Immature egg starts maturing Day 14 Highly vascularized Ovary releases a mature egg Days 15–28 Thickest and rich in blood vessels Waiting for a fertilised egg

options.label: A
options.text: The uterine lining will continue to thicken indefinitely to support a future zygote.

options.label: B
options.text: The mature unfertilised egg will implant itself into the uterine lining and remain dormant.

options.label: C
options.text: The thickened uterine lining will break down, leading directly to the events of Days 1–5.

options.label: D
options.text: The ovary will immediately release another mature egg on Day 15 to ensure pregnancy.

items.answer: The uterine lining reaches its maximum thickness between days 15 and 28 to prepare for the implantation of a fertilised egg. If fertilisation fails to occur, this nutrient-rich vascular preparation is no longer required. Consequently, the thickened lining breaks down and sheds, initiating the menstruation phase observed during days 1 to 5.

items.stem: As sperm travel from the testes through the vas deferens, glands secrete fluids to assist them. Which two glands are primarily responsible for adding fluid that nourishes the sperm and helps them remain active and motile?

options.label: B
options.text: Ovary and cervix

options.label: C
options.text: Urethra and scrotum

options.label: D

items.answer: During their journey through the male reproductive tract, sperm receive crucial secretions from specific accessory glands, namely the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland. These glandular fluids provide essential nutrients and a supportive liquid medium, which together nourish the sperm and significantly enhance their motility, ensuring they can actively swim toward the egg.

items.stem: In the human female reproductive system, the ovaries produce female germ cells (eggs). Through which specific anatomical structure does the mature egg travel to reach the uterus?

options.label: A
options.text: Cervix

options.label: B
options.text: Vagina

options.label: C
options.text: Oviduct (Fallopian tube)

options.label: D
options.text: Urethra

items.answer: In human females, once an ovary releases a mature egg during ovulation, it is caught and transported by the oviduct, also commonly known as the fallopian tube. This vital tube acts as a specialized passageway connecting the ovary to the uterus, and it is typically the precise location where fertilisation by a sperm occurs.

items.stem: Consider the following structural and functional differences between human male and female gametes based on the provided table. 1. Sperm is very small in size, whereas the egg is large. 2. Sperm is produced in millions, while eggs are produced in very few numbers. 3. Stored nutrients are abundant in sperm but absent in the egg. 4. Sperm is actively motile, whereas the egg is non-motile. Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.answer: Statements 1, 2, and 4 correctly describe the distinct differences between sperm and eggs. Sperm are small, motile, and produced in vast numbers. Statement 3 is entirely incorrect because the reality is exactly the opposite: the large female egg contains stored nutrients to support early embryonic development, whereas the tiny sperm lacks such reserves.

items.stem: In 1978, a significant milestone in medical science was achieved in India regarding artificial reproduction. Who pioneered India’s first test-tube baby through experimental in-vitro fertilisation (IVF)?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: P. Maheshwari

options.label: C
options.text: Subhash Mukhopadhyay

options.label: D
options.text: Gregor Mendel

items.answer: Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay was a pioneering medical researcher who successfully delivered India’s first test-tube baby, Kanupriya Agarwal (nicknamed Durga), in 1978. He achieved this remarkable feat through experimental In-Vitro Fertilisation (IVF), a sophisticated technique where an egg and sperm are combined outside the body in a specialized laboratory dish before implantation.

items.stem: Identify the correct sequential order of events that occur when a sperm successfully meets an egg in the human female reproductive tract. 1. The zygote implants into the thickened inner lining of the uterus. 2. Millions of sperm enter through the vagina during sexual intercourse. 3. A sperm successfully fuses with the egg to form a zygote. 4. The zygote undergoes a series of mitotic divisions while travelling. 5. Sperm swim upwards through the reproductive tract to reach the oviduct.
items.answer: The correct sequence begins with sperm entering the vagina (2) and swimming up to the oviduct (5). There, a single sperm fuses with the egg to create a zygote (3). This zygote immediately begins dividing mitotically as it travels down toward the uterus (4), where it finally implants into the nutrient-rich uterine lining (1).

items.stem: What is the fundamental biological importance of the process called gametogenesis in human reproduction?

options.label: A
options.text: It doubles the chromosome number in cells to provide extra genetic material.

options.label: B
options.text: It involves mitosis to produce millions of genetically identical gametes.

options.label: C
options.text: It reduces the number of chromosomes to half, ensuring the offspring maintains the standard 46 chromosomes.

options.label: D
options.text: It creates the thickened uterine lining required for immediate zygote implantation.

items.answer: Gametogenesis is the specialized formation of gametes in the testes and ovaries. It is fundamentally important because it utilizes meiosis, which reduces the diploid chromosome number by exactly half (from 46 to 23). When these haploid gametes fuse during fertilisation, they correctly restore the normal 46 chromosomes in the newly formed individual.

items.stem: Match the key stages of a typical 28-day menstrual cycle in List-I with their corresponding events in List-II. List-I (Cycle Stage) List-II (Event) P. Day 1–5 1. Ovary releases a mature egg Q. Day 6–14 2. Shedding of uterine lining (Menstruation) R. Day 14 3. Uterine lining becomes thicker and rich with blood vessels S. Day 15–28 4. Uterine lining gradually rebuilds while egg starts maturing
items.answer: During Days 1–5 (P), menstruation occurs as the old lining sheds (2). From Days 6–14 (Q), the lining rebuilds while a new egg matures (4). Around Day 14 (R), ovulation happens with the release of the egg (1). From Days 15–28 (S), the lining thickens further to prepare for potential pregnancy (3).

The body prepares the uterine lining every month specifically to receive and nourish a fertilised egg. If fertilisation fails to occur, this specialized preparation becomes redundant, leading to the shedding of the lining through the vagina.

items.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the stages of human pregnancy. 1. Pregnancy is divided into three stages called trimesters, lasting about nine months. 2. Major organs start forming in the developing embryo during the second trimester. 3. In the third trimester, the baby grows rapidly and prepares for life outside the womb. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 1 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 2 and 3 only

items.answer: Statements 1 and 3 are factually accurate descriptions of pregnancy stages. Statement 2 is incorrect because major organ formation begins much earlier. Specifically, the fundamental development of the embryo’s major organs occurs during the first two months of the first trimester, not delayed until the second trimester as the statement suggests.

items.stem: In humans, biological sex is determined by sex chromosomes. Since females have XX chromosomes and males have XY, which parent ultimately determines the biological sex of a newly conceived baby?

options.label: A
options.text: The mother, because she provides the larger egg containing essential nutrients.

options.label: B
options.text: The mother, because she always contributes an X chromosome.

options.label: C
options.text: The father, because he contributes either an X or a Y chromosome.

options.label: D
options.text: Both parents equally determine the sex through a blend of hormones.

items.answer: Human females possess XX chromosomes, meaning every egg always carries an X chromosome. Human males have XY chromosomes, producing sperm that carry either an X or a Y. Therefore, the father’s sperm dictates the biological sex: if an X-bearing sperm fertilises the egg, a female (XX) develops; if a Y-bearing sperm fertilises, a male (XY) develops.

items.stem: Consider the following recommended hygiene practices during menstruation. 1. Use biodegradable sanitary pads or menstrual cups. 2. Clean the genital area with strong soaps to eliminate all natural bacteria. 3. Change menstrual pads regularly, typically every 4–6 hours. Which of the given practices is/are medically advised for maintaining health?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: Statements 1 and 3 reflect excellent, recommended menstrual hygiene habits. Statement 2 is highly discouraged and incorrect. Washing the sensitive genital area with strong, harsh soaps can severely disrupt the natural, healthy bacterial balance, potentially leading to discomfort or infections. Only clean water is advised to maintain a safe and natural environment.

items.stem: As individuals grow through adolescence, they experience sexual maturation. However, what does it mean to be ‘emotionally mature’ as opposed to just sexually mature?

options.label: A
options.text: It means the body is fully physically capable of reproducing and bearing children.

options.label: B
options.text: It means handling feelings appropriately, communicating clearly, and making thoughtful decisions.

options.label: C
options.text: It means undergoing the physical production of sperm or the onset of menstrual cycles.

options.label: D
options.text: It means completely ignoring emotional responses to focus only on physical growth.

items.answer: While sexual maturity refers strictly to the physiological capability of reproduction (like sperm production or menstruation), emotional maturity is entirely psychological. Developing emotional maturity takes significantly longer and involves learning how to manage complex feelings, communicating effectively with others, and consistently making responsible, well-thought-out life choices during and beyond adolescence.

items.stem: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) are a serious health concern associated with unprotected sexual activity. Which of the following diseases is considered the ‘odd one out’ because it is currently not curable?

options.label: A
options.text: Gonorrhoea

options.label: B
options.text: Syphilis

options.label: C
options.text: HIV

options.label: D
options.text: Mild bacterial infections

items.answer: STIs are transmitted through intimate physical contact. While bacterial infections such as gonorrhoea and syphilis can generally be treated and cured with antibiotics, viral infections present greater challenges. Specifically, HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), which can eventually lead to AIDS, is a severe, life-long condition that currently has no permanent medical cure available.

items.stem: Consider the following statements regarding various contraceptive methods used to prevent unwanted pregnancies. 1. Condoms act as physical barriers that stop sperm from reaching the egg. 2. Oral pills alter hormonal balances to prevent the release of eggs from the ovaries. 3. Intra-Uterine Devices (IUDs) like Copper-T are completely free of any side effects. 4. Surgical methods block the vas deferens in males or fallopian tubes in females. Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.answer: Statements 1, 2, and 4 accurately describe barrier, hormonal, and surgical contraceptive methods. Statement 3 is incorrect. While Intra-Uterine Devices (IUDs) like the Copper-T are highly effective at preventing pregnancy, they are not completely without issues; they can sometimes cause irritation in the uterus, leading to discomfort or unexpected bleeding in some users.

items.stem: Which of the following statements incorrectly describes the function or placement of the Intra-Uterine Device (IUD) known as Copper-T?

options.label: A
options.text: It is placed inside the female’s uterus by a healthcare professional.

options.label: B
options.text: It functions effectively as a barrier method to trap sperm in the vagina.

options.label: C
options.text: It is used to avoid unwanted pregnancy over a long period.

options.label: D
options.text: It may sometimes cause irritation to the inner lining of the uterus.

items.answer: The statement is incorrect because a Copper-T is an Intra-Uterine Device, not a barrier method. Barrier methods, like condoms, physically block sperm in the vagina or cervix. In contrast, an IUD is inserted deep into the uterus, where it alters the internal environment, preventing sperm viability and inhibiting the implantation of an embryo.

items.stem: Indian scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow, developed a revolutionary contraceptive method provided through the National Family Planning Programme. What was this specific invention?

options.label: A
options.text: The world’s first biodegradable sanitary pad

options.label: B
options.text: The world’s first surgical robotic device for blocking fallopian tubes

options.label: C
options.text: The world’s first non-steroidal and non-hormonal oral contraceptive pill

options.label: D
options.text: A highly advanced, irritation-free copper IUD

items.answer: Scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow made a major global breakthrough by developing the world’s first non-steroidal and non-hormonal oral contraceptive pill. Designed to be taken just once a week, it is highly effective while avoiding common hormonal side effects like weight gain, nausea, or debilitating headaches.
